title: 2015 AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: Claudia has \(12\) coins, each of which is a \(5\)-cent coin or a \(10\)-cent coin. There are exactly \(17\) different values that can be obtained as combinations of one or more of her coins. How many \(10\)-cent coins does Claudia have?

solutions.text:
Let the number of \(5\)-cent coins be \(x\) and the number of \(10\)-cent coins be \(12 - x.\)

If \(x=0,\) the only possible values are \(10,20,\ldots,120\) cents, giving just \(12\) values. Hence \(x>0.\) Having at least one \(5\)-cent coin then makes every multiple of \(5\) from \(5\) through the total value \[5x+10(12-x)=120-5x\] obtainable.

There are \(24 - x\) such multiples of \(5,\) which means that \(x = 7\) to get \(17\) possible different values.

The number of \(10\)-cent coins is therefore \(12 - 7 = 5.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Count possible values in units of five cents
If there are \(x\) nickels, the largest value is \(120-5x\) cents
